FX theme
Rising US bond yields and severe tech sector headwinds dominate the session, placing significant downward pressure on high-beta commodity currencies. Meanwhile, safe-haven demand supports the US dollar and Japanese yen while risk assets like the S&P 500 retreat 0.35 percent.

Dollar read
The DXY trades at 103.14 with a strong weekly gain of 1.5 percent, bolstered by US 10-year yields jumping 24.4 basis points over the week to 5.103 percent. Commodity currencies suffer notably, led by AUD/USD dropping 0.71 percent to 0.6794 amid the broader risk-off environment.

Crosses
Yen crosses are broadly weaker as AUD/JPY drops 0.69 percent to 108.539 and EUR/JPY slips 0.26 percent to 176.757, reflecting defensive positioning. Euro crosses show mixed performance with EUR/AUD gaining 0.43 percent to 1.6284 as the Australian dollar underperforms.

Potential scenarios
▼ Bearish · EUR/US

Key risks

• Ongoing fallout from major tech sector disruptions and equity market weakness could accelerate safe-haven flows.
